You are given a 2D Strip Packing Problem (2SP).
The input describes a rectangular strip with a fixed width and a variable or limited height, along with a list of item types, each specified by a fixed width and height.

**You must place exactly one copy of each item type into the strip.** **All items must be axis-aligned, lie entirely within the strip boundaries, and must not overlap.**

Each item is positioned by specifying the coordinates of its bottom-left corner within the strip. The horizontal coordinate indicates the distance from the left boundary, and the vertical coordinate indicates the distance from the bottom boundary. The height of an item refers to the vertical size of the rectangle itself.

The objective is to minimize the used height of the packing, defined as the highest vertical position reached by the top edge of any placed item.

You will receive the instance in the following format:
{{INSTANCE_INPUT}}

Return your placement in **exactly** the following JSON format:
```json
{
  "solution": [
    {"item_type": <item_type_id>, "x": 0, "y": 0, "width": 10, "height": 5},
    ...
  ]
}
```
Each object represents one placed rectangle, defined by its bottom-left corner coordinates and its size.
Use the item_type identifiers exactly as they appear in the input.
**Do not include explanations, comments, or any extra keys.**

contexts.text: [BASELINE] Canonical task wording.

Please arrange a single copy of every rectangular furniture panel inside a moving van with a fixed internal width so that each panel is aligned with the van walls, none of the panels overlap and all panels lie completely inside, and arrange them to keep the highest top edge as low as possible.

Position a single instance of each rectangular advertisement module within a fixed width website sidebar, keeping every module aligned with the sidebar edges, preventing overlaps and keeping all modules fully inside, and minimize the total vertical extent of the stacked modules.

As curator, place a single copy of each rectangular painting onto a narrow display wall of fixed width with all paintings aligned to the wall frame, no paintings overlapping and every painting fully within the wall area, and aim to keep the display height used as small as possible.

Organize a single unit of each rectangular crate type into a racking bay that has a fixed width, with all crates placed flush to the rack sides and not rotated, ensuring there is no overlap and all crates remain inside the bay, and stack them to minimize the maximum height reached.

Please fit a single copy of every rectangular book spine upright on a shallow shelf with a fixed width, keeping spines parallel to the shelf edges and inside the shelf boundaries without overlapping, and arrange them to use as little vertical shelf height as possible.

Load a single bolt of each rectangular fabric type into a storage chute of fixed width so that every bolt is aligned with the chute sides, bolts do not overlap and each bolt lies fully inside the chute, and position them to minimize the overall stacking height.

Mount a single copy of each rectangular sign panel onto a vertical signboard of fixed width, keeping panels aligned with the board edges and not overlapping while remaining entirely on the board, and place them to keep the topmost panel as low as possible.

Please lay out a single copy of each rectangular poster print on a printing roll of fixed usable width, aligning each poster with the roll edges, avoiding any overlap and keeping all posters fully on the roll, and minimize the highest vertical position reached by any poster.

Arrange a single unit of each rectangular planter box along a balcony ledge of fixed width, placing boxes edge aligned with the ledge, ensuring boxes do not overlap and all are fully on the ledge, and space them to minimize the maximum vertical stacking height.

Position a single copy of each flat scenic element into a stage wing that has a fixed width, keeping elements aligned with the wing borders and preventing overlaps while ensuring all elements fit inside, and arrange them to minimize the overall used height.

Please place a single stack of each rectangular clothing bundle into a narrow display column of fixed width so that each bundle is aligned with the column sides, bundles do not overlap and remain entirely inside, and organize them to keep the topmost edge as low as possible.

Insert a single copy of each flat hardware panel into a server rack bay with a fixed width, keeping panels aligned to the rack rails and preventing any overlap while ensuring each panel sits fully within the bay, and arrange them to minimize the maximum vertical position used.

Mount a single copy of each rectangular solar panel onto a tower face of fixed width, keeping panels aligned with the tower edges and not overlapping while remaining fully on the face, and position them to minimize the total vertical span covered.

Place a single unit of each advertisement board onto a roadside column that has a fixed width, aligning boards with the column edges, ensuring boards do not overlap and are completely on the column, and arrange them to keep the highest board edge as low as possible.

Pack a single copy of each rectangular product box into a shipping sleeve of fixed width, placing boxes aligned with the sleeve walls and preventing overlap while keeping all boxes inside, and pack them so the sleeve height used is as small as possible.

Lay out a single instance of each rectangular vendor stall graphic along a corridor wall of fixed width, keeping graphics aligned to the wall edges and non overlapping while fully inside the wall area, and arrange them to minimize the total vertical extent.

Load a single copy of each rectangular timber panel into a delivery crate that has a fixed width, aligning panels with the crate sides and avoiding any overlap while ensuring all panels fit inside, and stack them to use the least possible vertical space.

Organize a single tray of each rectangular sample type inside an incubator chamber of fixed width so that trays are aligned with the chamber walls, do not overlap and sit fully inside the chamber, and arrange them to minimize the highest tray top.

Please place a single copy of each rectangular shelf label within a narrow header strip of fixed width, aligning labels to the strip edges and preventing overlaps while keeping all labels fully on the strip, and position them to keep the used height as small as possible.

Arrange a single instance of each rectangular content card in a fixed width mobile app column, keeping cards aligned with the column edges and non overlapping while remaining fully within the column, and order them to minimize the overall vertical length of the feed.

Help me arrange a set of framed photos on a horizontal display board of fixed width so that each frame is placed exactly once without tilting, no two frames overlap, every frame lies entirely inside the board, and the vertical extent up to the top edge of the highest frame is as small as possible; for each frame give the distance from the left edge and the distance from the bottom that locate its bottom-left corner.

Help position a set of folded garments inside a fixed width closet slot so that each garment is placed exactly once, none are rotated or tilted, they do not overlap, each stays fully within the slot, and the maximum vertical reach of any garment is minimized; for each garment give the distance from the left side and from the closet floor to its bottom-left corner.

Arrange a collection of rectangular ceramic tiles on a fixed width backsplash area so each tile is used exactly once, every tile is aligned with the backsplash sides, tiles do not overlap and remain inside the area, and the highest top of any tile is as small as possible; state for each tile how far it is from the left edge and from the bottom edge to locate its bottom-left corner.

As an exhibition curator, place a set of art panels on a display strip of fixed width such that each panel is hung exactly once, panels are upright with edges parallel to the strip, none overlap, each panel is fully inside the strip, and the vertical span to the highest panel top is minimized; for every panel give the leftward distance from the strip edge and the upward distance from the bottom edge for its bottom-left corner.

Please plan how to fit a group of rectangular cardboard samples into a fixed width display tray so that each sample goes in exactly once, all samples are axis aligned, they do not overlap, all lie inside the tray, and the used height up to the topmost sample is as small as possible; for each sample provide the offset from the tray left boundary and the offset from the tray bottom to its bottom-left corner.

Help me pack unique gift boxes onto a fixed width vertical rack so that every box is placed exactly once with faces parallel to the rack edges, no boxes overlap, all boxes remain within rack limits, and the highest top edge among boxes is kept as low as possible; give for each box the horizontal distance from the left rack edge and the vertical distance from the rack base to its bottom-left corner.

Help me position a collection of wooden planks on a fixed width storage ledge so that each plank is stored exactly once, all planks lie with edges parallel to the ledge edges, they do not overlap, each fits entirely inside the ledge, and the highest topmost edge is as low as possible; for every plank specify the distance from the ledge left edge and from the ledge floor to its bottom-left corner.

Plan placement of a batch of rectangular fabric swatches on a fixed width mounting board so that each swatch is attached exactly once, swatches are aligned with board edges, they do not overlap, each remains fully inside the board, and the total occupied height up to the tallest swatch is minimized; for each swatch state the distance from the board left boundary and the distance from the bottom boundary to its bottom-left corner.

As a vendor, organize a set of rectangular price tags on a fixed width display strip so that every tag is used exactly once, tags are placed straight with edges parallel to the strip, no tag overlaps another, all tags stay inside the strip, and the vertical extent to the highest tag top is minimized; supply for each tag the left offset and the bottom offset that locate its bottom-left corner.

Help me layout a collection of rectangular recipe cards on a fixed width kitchen wall panel so that each card is placed exactly once without rotation, cards do not overlap, each card fits entirely within the panel, and the overall height measured to the highest card top is as small as possible; for each card provide how far it sits from the left panel edge and how far from the bottom panel edge to its bottom-left corner.

As a carpenter, arrange several rectangular cabinet doors on a fixed width vertical test stand so that each door is positioned exactly once with its edges parallel to the stand, doors do not overlap and are fully inside the stand, and the maximum top edge height among doors is minimized; for each door give the horizontal measurement from the left side and the vertical measurement from the bottom that mark its bottom-left corner.

As a studio manager, place a group of rectangular canvases on a fixed width hanging rail so that each canvas hangs exactly once, canvases are straight and aligned with the rail, none overlap, each stays inside the rail boundaries, and the used vertical space up to the tallest canvas top is minimized; provide for each canvas the leftward offset from the rail edge and the upward offset from the rail base for its bottom-left corner.

Help me fit several rectangular mat boards into a fixed width vertical slot so that each mat board is inserted exactly once, all boards are placed without tilting, they do not overlap, each remains fully inside the slot, and the highest top edge among the boards is minimized; for each mat board state its distance from the left boundary and its distance from the bottom boundary to the bottom-left corner.

A retail visual merchandiser needs you to arrange a single copy of every rectangular fabric sample on a wall strip that has a fixed width by specifying where the bottom-left corner of each sample sits relative to the left and bottom boundaries so that all samples remain axis aligned, fully inside the strip, do not overlap, and the total vertical extent used is minimized.

A glass workshop asks you to lay a single copy of each rectangular window pane onto a stacking board of fixed width by choosing the bottom-left coordinate for each pane relative to the left and bottom edges so that panes are axis aligned, entirely inside the board, never overlap, and the topmost edge height across all panes is minimized.

A graphic designer requests that you position a single copy of every rectangular sticker on a roll of fixed width by picking the horizontal and vertical offsets from the left and bottom margins for each sticker so that stickers remain axis aligned, inside the roll boundaries, do not overlap, and the total height used is as small as possible.

A carpenter asks you to fit a single copy of each rectangular shelf backing onto a fixed width board by determining the bottom-left placement coordinates from the left and bottom sides such that each backing is axis aligned, fully within the board, non overlapping, and the highest vertical reach of any backing is minimized.

A shipping planner asks you to arrange a single copy of each rectangular parcel on a pallet area of fixed width by choosing the bottom-left position for each parcel measured from the pallet's left and bottom edges so that parcels are axis aligned, contained within the pallet, do not overlap, and the maximum stack height of any parcel top is minimized.

An exhibition installer wants you to place a single copy of each rectangular banner onto a vertical mounting strip of fixed width by assigning horizontal and vertical coordinates from the left and bottom boundaries for each banner so that banners are axis aligned, fully inside the strip, do not overlap, and the greatest height reached by any banner is as small as possible.

A wallpaper planner asks you to set a single copy of every rectangular pattern panel onto a fixed width wall strip by determining for each panel its bottom-left anchor point from the left and bottom edges so that panels are axis aligned, lie entirely within the strip, never overlap, and the highest top edge among them is minimized.

A store window stylist needs you to place a single copy of each rectangular prop on a display strip of fixed width by choosing the horizontal and vertical offsets from the left and bottom edges for each prop so that props remain axis aligned, stay fully inside the strip, do not overlap, and the maximum vertical extent used is as small as possible.

A packaging designer asks you to position a single copy of each rectangular insert on a shipping sleeve of fixed width by specifying the bottom-left coordinates from the left and bottom edges for every insert so that inserts are axis aligned, lie completely inside the sleeve, do not overlap, and the topmost height across all inserts is minimized.

A craft fair coordinator asks you to arrange a single copy of each rectangular display mat on a booth strip of fixed width by assigning horizontal and vertical positions measured from the left and bottom edges so that mats are axis aligned, fully within the strip, do not overlap, and the overall height used is as low as possible.

A greenhouse planner needs you to place a single copy of every rectangular seed tray on a narrow bench of fixed width by deciding the bottom-left location for each tray from the left and bottom edges so that trays are axis aligned, remain entirely inside the bench area, do not overlap, and the highest top level of any tray is minimized.

A printing operator wants you to place a single copy of each rectangular print job on a feeder strip with fixed width by specifying the bottom-left coordinates from the left and bottom boundaries for each job so that prints stay axis aligned, entirely inside the feeder, do not overlap, and the topmost printed edge is as low as possible.

A display designer asks you to fit a single copy of each rectangular product board onto a hanging strip of fixed width by assigning horizontal and vertical placement measured from the left and bottom edges so that boards are axis aligned, fully within the strip, never overlap, and the maximum height reached by any board is minimized.

An events crew asks you to lay out a single copy of each rectangular floor graphic along a runner of fixed width by selecting for every graphic the horizontal and vertical offsets from the left and bottom edges so that graphics are axis aligned, lie entirely within the runner, do not overlap, and the greatest vertical reach among them is as small as possible.

Lay out a single piece of every rectangular fabric pattern along a cutting bed that has a fixed usable width by arranging patterns with their sides parallel to the bed edges so they do not overlap and lie completely within the bed, and make the total used length in the stacking direction as small as possible.

Place a single panel of every rectangular glass sheet into a vertical storage slot that has a fixed width, keeping each sheet upright and aligned with the slot edges so they do not overlap and remain entirely inside the slot, while minimizing the tallest top edge among the stored sheets.

Arrange a single sample of each rectangular tile type on a rigid strip of fixed width by positioning tiles with edges parallel to the strip borders without overlapping and keeping them fully within the strip, aiming to minimize the highest vertical extent of the arrangement.

As a web sidebar designer, fit a single rectangle of each content block into a sidebar of fixed width by placing blocks upright with edges aligned to the sidebar so they never overlap and always remain inside the sidebar, and reduce the total vertical scroll length used.

Configure a shop window by placing a single copy of each rectangular merchandise display within a fixed-width display band, positioning items with sides parallel to the band boundaries so they do not overlap and stay fully within the band, with the objective of minimizing how tall the overall arrangement becomes.

Fit a single plate of each rectangular metal part onto a plating rack that has a fixed width by setting plates with edges parallel to rack edges so they do not overlap and stay completely within the rack, while minimizing the maximum height reached by any plate.

Arrange a single sample board of every rectangular flooring plank along a fixed-width corridor display by placing boards with their sides parallel to corridor edges without overlap and fully inside the corridor bounds, with the goal of minimizing the overall vertical reach of the display.

As a carpenter, lay out a single template of each rectangular cupboard door onto a board with fixed width by orienting templates with edges parallel to the board and preventing any overlap while keeping all templates inside the board, and minimize the highest vertical position occupied.

Fit a single rectangular photograph of each size into a fixed-width portrait column by positioning photos upright with edges parallel to the column sides so they do not overlap and remain entirely within the column, and minimize the total vertical space required.

Arrange a single rectangular poster of each event onto a fixed-width street pole banner by keeping posters oriented upright and aligned with the pole edges so they do not overlap and lie completely within the banner, with the objective of minimizing how tall the packed banner becomes.

Organize a single rectangular wood veneer sheet of each type on a laminating strip that has fixed width by placing sheets with their sides parallel to the strip edges so they never overlap and remain entirely within the strip, and minimize the tallest top edge among the placed sheets.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The usable internal width of the moving van measured left-to-right along the floor. All panels' horizontal positions (x of their bottom-left corner) plus their panel_width must lie within [0, van_interior_width]; no panel may extend past the van side walls.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The usable internal height of the van measured from the floor to the ceiling. Any panel's top edge is its vertical placement (y of bottom-left) plus its panel_height and must not exceed this ceiling. If the instance models an unbounded strip, this value may be set very large to indicate no practical ceiling; the packing objective is to minimize the maximum top edge reached.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a furniture panel (left-to-right). Panels are axis-aligned and cannot be rotated, so panel_width plus the panel's horizontal placement determines whether it fits between the van walls.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size of a furniture panel. The panel's top edge equals its vertical placement (distance from the floor to the panel's bottom edge) plus panel_height; the packing score is the highest such top edge across all panels.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier or label for each distinct furniture panel type. Exactly one panel with each panel_id must be placed inside the van without overlap.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: Fixed horizontal width of the website sidebar (e.g., in pixels). Every ad module must fit inside this width; valid x (left) placement values run from 0 to sidebar_width - ad_width.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: Vertical height of the sidebar used as an upper bound on placements. If the instance has no fixed height, this can be set to a very large value or treated as infinite; the solver still aims to minimize the actual used height (the highest top edge of any ad).

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: Horizontal size of a single advertisement module. Must be no larger than sidebar_width and determines how much horizontal space the module consumes when placed.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: Vertical size of a single advertisement module. Placing an ad at vertical coordinate y makes its top edge at y + ad_height, which contributes to the packing's used height.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for the advertisement module (e.g., 'promo_1'). Use this id to refer to the module when specifying its bottom-left placement coordinates and constraints.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed horizontal width of the gallery display wall (distance from the left to the right frame). Each painting's horizontal position plus its painting_width must not exceed this wall width.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The vertical extent available on the wall for placing paintings. If the wall height is not fixed this value can act as an upper bound or a large sentinel; the used height of the arrangement is the maximum (vertical offset + painting_height) over all paintings.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a painting. When placed at horizontal offset x from the left frame, the painting occupies [x, x + painting_width] and must lie entirely within the display_wall_width.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size of a painting. When placed at vertical offset y from the bottom frame, the painting occupies [y, y + painting_height]; the objective is to minimize the maximum of these top edges across all paintings.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for each painting type (one copy of each must be placed). Used to reference dimensions and placement for that particular painting.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: Internal usable width of the racking bay (left-to-right). All crate horizontal positions are measured from the bay's left wall and every crate's width must fit within this value (horizontal coordinate + crate_width ≤ rack_bay_width).

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: Vertical capacity limit of the racking bay measured from the floor. If the instance models an unbounded stacking height, this may be set to a large value or ignored; otherwise it is the maximum allowed top edge height for any crate (vertical coordinate + crate_height ≤ rack_bay_height).

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: Horizontal size of a crate (left-to-right). Crate widths are fixed, crates are not rotated, and each crate's horizontal placement must ensure it remains within the rack_bay_width.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: Vertical size of a crate (floor-to-top). The top edge of a crate equals its vertical placement coordinate plus this crate_height; the objective is to minimize the maximum such top edge over all crates.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for a crate type (one unit of each must be placed). This label distinguishes crates so the solver places exactly one copy of each crate_type_id in the bay.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The usable horizontal width of the shelf (left-to-right). Each spine's x-coordinate (left edge) plus its spine_width must not exceed this value.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The vertical limit of the shelf space (distance from the shelf bottom to the top boundary). All spines' top edges (y + spine_height) must lie at or below this height. If the instance minimizes used height, this can be treated as an upper bound (possibly a large number); the actual used shelf height is the maximum top edge among placed spines.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal thickness of a book spine (how much left-right shelf width it occupies). When placed, the spine's left x-position plus this value determines its right edge.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical height of a book spine (how tall it is). When placed, the spine's bottom y-position plus this value gives its top edge; the objective is to minimize the maximum of these top edges.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for each book spine (for example a title or index). Exactly one copy of each book_spine_id must be placed on the shelf without overlap.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The interior horizontal width of the storage chute (distance between the chute's inside vertical walls). Every bolt's horizontal placement plus its bolt_width must not exceed this value; all bolts are aligned with the chute sides.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The vertical interior height limit of the chute measured from the floor to the top inside surface. If the chute has no fixed cap, this field represents an upper bounding height (a large number) but otherwise no bolt top may exceed this limit. The packing quality is measured by the actual highest bolt top (which should be minimized).

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a single fabric bolt when placed flat in the chute (left-to-right). This dimension, together with the bolt's x-coordinate, must stay within the chute_inner_width.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size of a bolt (bottom-to-top). For a bolt placed at vertical position y, its top reaches y + bolt_height; the packing objective is to minimize the maximum of these top positions across all bolts.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for the fabric bolt type (for example a label or SKU). The instance requires placing exactly one bolt of each listed bolt_type_id into the chute.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed horizontal width of the vertical signboard (distance from left to right edge). All panels' widths must fit within this span when placed; x-coordinates range from 0 to this value minus the panel width.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The vertical extent of the mounted layout on the signboard measured from the board bottom to the highest panel top. In this scenario this represents the height to be minimized (the topmost panel's top edge); if a fixed board height is given it serves as an upper bound.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a specific sign panel (how much left‑to‑right space it occupies). This determines how far it can be placed from the left edge (x coordinate) so it remains entirely on the board.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size of a specific sign panel (how tall the rectangle is). A panel placed with bottom at y has its top at y + panel_height, which is used to compute the used_board_height.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier or name for each sign panel type. Exactly one panel with this id must be mounted; identifiers distinguish panels when specifying positions.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed horizontal usable width of the printing roll. Every poster's horizontal position x must satisfy 0 ≤ x ≤ roll_usable_width − poster_width, and no poster's width may exceed this value.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The vertical usable length of the roll (maximum allowed height). If the roll height is unbounded or variable for the instance, this can be null or a very large value; otherwise it is the top-edge limit that no poster (y + poster_height) may exceed.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: Horizontal size of a poster, measured parallel to the roll edges. Used to check fitting within roll_usable_width and to constrain the poster's x-coordinate so the poster stays fully on the roll.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: Vertical size of a poster. The poster's top edge is y + poster_height; the objective is to minimize the maximum of these top edges (the used roll height).

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for the poster type (e.g., name, SKU, or index). Associates each width/height pair with a specific poster to place and to report placement coordinates for.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The usable horizontal length of the balcony ledge measured from the left edge to the right edge; every planter's x-position plus its planter_width must be less than or equal to this value so no planter hangs off the ledge.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The vertical limit of the available stacking space measured from the ledge bottom upward; no planter's top (y-position + planter_height) may exceed this. If the instance models an unbounded vertical space, this may be set to a very large value or treated as effectively infinite while the objective is to minimize the used height.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a planter (left-to-right). When placing a planter, its x-coordinate plus this planter_width determines how far it extends across the ledge and must fit within ledge_width.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size of a planter. A planter placed at vertical position y has its top at y + planter_height; the packing's objective is to minimize the maximum of these top positions.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for each planter type (exactly one of each identifier must be placed). Used to link a planter's dimensions to its placement coordinates.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed horizontal width of the stage wing (distance from the left wall to the right wall). All element bottom-left x-coordinates must be chosen so the whole element lies within [0, wing_width], i.e. x ∈ [0, wing_width - element_width].

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: An upper bound on the usable vertical space in the wing (distance from the floor to the ceiling). If the wing has no fixed ceiling, this can be set to a sufficiently large value. All element bottom-left y-coordinates must satisfy 0 ≤ y ≤ wing_height_limit - element_height. The packing objective is to minimize the maximum top-edge height (y + element_height) across all elements.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a scenic element when placed axis-aligned in the wing. This value determines how much horizontal space the element occupies and must be no larger than wing_width.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size of a scenic element. For an element placed with bottom-left corner at vertical coordinate y, its top edge is at y + element_height; these top edges define the used height to be minimized.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier (name or index) for the scenic element type. Exactly one copy of each element_id must be placed inside the wing; use this id to associate the element's element_width and element_height with its placement coordinates.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed internal horizontal width of the narrow display column (distance between the left and right walls). Every bundle's horizontal size (bundle_width) and its placement x-coordinate must keep the bundle fully inside these walls (x + bundle_width ≤ display_column_width).

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The vertical limit (ceiling) of the display column measured from the floor. Bundles must lie entirely below this height (y + bundle_height ≤ display_column_max_height). If the instance models an unbounded strip, this value represents an available upper bound for feasibility checks; the actual objective is to minimize the highest top edge among placed bundles.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a folded clothing bundle. This determines how much horizontal space the bundle occupies inside the column; it must fit between the column walls when placed at its chosen x-coordinate.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical thickness (height) of a folded clothing bundle. When placed at vertical coordinate y, its top edge is at y + bundle_height; the packing objective is to minimize the maximum of these top-edge heights across all bundles.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for each clothing bundle type. Exactly one bundle with this id must be placed in the column (no duplicates or omissions).

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The usable horizontal width of the server rack bay measured between the rails (units consistent with panel widths). Each panel's x (left) coordinate must be >= 0 and x + panel_width must be <= bay_interior_width.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: An optional upper bound on the bay's usable vertical interior measured from the bay floor to the ceiling. If the bay height is fixed, this is the maximum allowed used height; if unbounded, this can be set very large or treated as absent. Each panel's y (bottom) coordinate must be >= 0 and y + panel_height must be <= this value when provided.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The panel's horizontal size (how far it spans left-to-right across the bay). Must be expressed in the same units as bay_interior_width and cannot exceed that width for a valid placement.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The panel's vertical size (how tall it is). A panel placed at vertical coordinate y occupies height from y up to y + panel_height; the packing objective is to minimize the maximum of these top edges.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for the panel type (for example a part or model name). Exactly one panel with each panel_id must be placed in the bay.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed horizontal width of the tower face where panels are mounted. Each panel's x (left) coordinate must be between 0 and (tower_face_width - panel_width) so the panel lies fully on the face.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: An optional vertical limit of the tower face (the available mounting height). If provided, every panel's top edge (bottom_y + panel_height) must not exceed this value; if the problem treats height as unbounded, interpret this field as 'no preset limit'.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a solar panel. Used to enforce that the panel fits within the tower_face_width and to prevent horizontal overlap with other panels.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size of a solar panel. The top edge equals bottom_y + panel_height; the objective is to minimize the maximum of these top edges across all panels.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for each distinct solar panel that must be mounted. Exactly one panel with each panel_id must be placed on the tower face.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed horizontal width of the roadside column (the usable left-to-right space). All advertisement boards' widths must fit within this measurement when placed flush against the column edges.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The available vertical space on the column. This represents an upper bound on mounting height (if the column height is effectively unbounded for the instance, this can be treated as 'no explicit limit'). The packing objective is to minimize the highest top edge of any board within this limit.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of an individual advertisement board. When placed, the board's left-right offset plus this width must not exceed the column_width.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size of an individual advertisement board. The board's bottom placement plus this height determines its top edge, which contributes to the overall used height to be minimized.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for each advertisement board type (one distinct board of each id must be mounted). Use this id to refer to the board when assigning its left-right offset and bottom position on the column.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The usable internal width of the shipping sleeve measured between its left and right walls. This is the fixed horizontal span boxes must fit within; for any box, its placement x-coordinate must be in [0, sleeve_inner_width - box_width], and no box width may exceed this value.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The maximum allowable height for the sleeve (the vertical limit). In instances where height is unbounded, this can be treated as a sufficiently large cap or null; otherwise it bounds box placements so every box's top edge (y + box_height) must be ≤ sleeve_max_height. The objective, however, is to minimize the actual used sleeve height defined by the highest box top.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal dimension of a product box (how far it extends across the sleeve). Boxes are axis-aligned and this width determines allowable x positions and overlap avoidance when placed against other boxes or sleeve walls.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical dimension of a product box (how tall it is). A box placed with bottom-left y coordinate contributes a top edge at y + box_height; the packing height objective is the maximum of these top edges.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for the product box type (e.g., SKU or model). Exactly one box of each product_box_id must be placed inside the sleeve, with identity used to reference its width, height, and placement.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed horizontal span of the corridor wall where all vendor graphics are hung. All graphic left-edge x-coordinates must be between 0 and this width minus the graphic's width; units match item widths.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The vertical extent available on the wall for placing graphics. If a maximum is specified, no graphic top may exceed this value; if the layout height is variable/unbounded, this field can be treated as a large or unspecified limit while the objective minimizes the actually used height (the highest top edge).

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a vendor's rectangular graphic measured along the wall; it determines how much of the wall width that graphic occupies and must fit entirely within [0, wall_width] when placed.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size of a vendor's rectangular graphic measured from its bottom edge (height from the floor). The top of the graphic is at its bottom y-coordinate plus this height and contributes to the used display height.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for each vendor's graphic (one instance per id). Use this to refer to each distinct rectangle that must be placed exactly once along the wall.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The usable internal width of the delivery crate measured left-to-right. This is the horizontal limit: for any panel, its bottom-left x-coordinate plus its panel_width must not exceed this value.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The internal height available in the crate measured floor-to-ceiling. In instances where height is unbounded this represents the allowable maximum (may be treated as infinite); panel placements must not place any top edge above this limit.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal dimension of a timber panel (left-to-right). Used to check that the panel fits within the crate width and to prevent horizontal overlap with other panels.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical thickness/height of a timber panel (bottom-to-top). The top edge of a placed panel is bottom_left_y + panel_height and determines the packing's used height and vertical non-overlap constraints.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier (SKU or label) for the panel type. Exactly one copy of each panel_id must be placed into the crate.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed internal width of the incubator chamber (distance between the left and right walls). All tray horizontal sizes and x-coordinates are measured against this value; every tray must lie entirely within 0 and this width.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The usable interior height of the incubator. If provided, it is an upper bound that tray top edges cannot exceed; if not provided or set to a very large value, treat the height as effectively unbounded and minimize the resulting used height instead.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal (left-to-right) size of a single sample tray. When placing a tray, its bottom-left x-coordinate plus this tray_width must not exceed the incubator_interior_width. Trays are axis-aligned and may not be rotated.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical (bottom-to-top) size of a single sample tray. A tray's top edge equals its bottom-left y-coordinate plus this tray_height; the objective is to minimize the maximum top edge across all trays.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for each tray type (one tray of each id must be placed). Use this id to reference the tray's tray_width, tray_height, and placement.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed horizontal width of the header strip (in the same length units as label sizes). All label x‑positions must be chosen so each label lies entirely within [0, header_strip_width]; i.e., x + label_width ≤ header_strip_width. This is the narrow fixed width the designer must pack into.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The vertical extent available for the header. If given as a finite number it is the top boundary labels cannot cross (y + label_height ≤ header_strip_height_limit). If treated as unbounded (or set very large) it indicates no preset upper bound and the solver's objective is to minimize the used height (the highest top edge of any label).

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a shelf label. This determines how much horizontal space the label occupies and constrains valid x placements (must satisfy 0 ≤ x ≤ header_strip_width − label_width).

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size of a shelf label. The label's top edge is at y + label_height; the arrangement's used height is the maximum of these top edges across all labels.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for each distinct shelf label type. Exactly one copy of each label_id must be placed in the header; identifiers are used to reference sizes and placement decisions for that label.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: Fixed horizontal width of the mobile app column (in the same units as card widths). All cards must lie within these left/right boundaries and be aligned with the column edges.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: Vertical limit of the column (in the same units as card heights). If the feed height is unbounded, treat this as a practical upper bound or screen height; the solver's objective is to minimize the actual used feed height (the highest top edge of any card), which will be ≤ this value when a limit is imposed.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: Horizontal size of a content card. The card's left coordinate must be ≥ 0 and its left + card_width_px must be ≤ column_width_px so the card stays fully inside the column.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: Vertical size of a content card. When placed at a vertical position y, the card occupies vertical interval [y, y + card_height_px] and contributes to the feed's total height via its top edge y + card_height_px.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for the card type (e.g., a content template or ad slot). Exactly one instance of each card_id must be placed in the column.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed horizontal width of the display board (distance from the left edge to the right edge). Every frame's left x-coordinate plus its frame_width must be ≤ this value so the frame lies entirely inside the board.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The vertical capacity of the display board measured from the bottom edge upward. If the studio provides a fixed maximum height, this is that limit and every frame's bottom y-coordinate plus its frame_height must be ≤ this value; if no fixed limit is given, treat this as unbounded and minimize the highest top edge reached by any frame.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a single framed photo. Used to check horizontal fit and non-overlap: a frame placed at x has right edge at x + frame_width.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size of a single framed photo. A frame placed at y has top edge at y + frame_height; the maximum of these top edges over all frames is the display's used height to be minimized.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for each one-of-a-kind frame (for example a label or index). Exactly one placement must be provided for each frame_id.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: Inner horizontal width of the closet slot (distance from the left wall to the right wall). All garment x-positions (distance from left) plus their garment_width must lie within [0, slot_width]. Units match the garment dimensions.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: Vertical distance available in the slot from floor to ceiling. If the slot has no fixed ceiling this may be treated as unbounded or set to a large value; otherwise every garment y-position (distance from floor) plus its garment_height must be ≤ slot_height_limit. The packing objective minimizes the highest top edge used.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: Horizontal width of the folded garment measured left-to-right. The garment must be placed axis-aligned (no rotation), so its x-coordinate + garment_width must not exceed slot_width.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: Vertical height (thickness) of the folded garment measured bottom-to-top. A garment's y-coordinate (distance from the closet floor) plus garment_height determines its top edge, which contributes to the used height objective.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier or name for this garment type. Exactly one item with this garment_id must be placed in the slot; identifiers distinguish garments for placement and non-overlap constraints.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed horizontal width of the backsplash area (distance from the left edge to the right edge). All tiles' left-bottom x-coordinate plus their tile_width must be ≤ this value; no tile may extend beyond this width.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The vertical extent of the backsplash area. If provided, it is the upper boundary that tiles must not cross (y + tile_height ≤ this value). If unspecified or null in the instance, it indicates the backsplash height is unbounded and the solver should minimize the used height (the maximum top edge of any tile).

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a ceramic tile (left-to-right). Tiles are placed axis-aligned and cannot be rotated; a tile placed at horizontal position x occupies [x, x + tile_width) and must fit within the backsplash_width.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size of a ceramic tile (bottom-to-top). A tile placed at vertical position y has its top at y + tile_height; the objective is to minimize the maximum of these top values across all tiles (the used backsplash height).

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for each tile type (e.g., a label or index). Use this id to refer to the specific tile when reporting its bottom-left placement coordinates (distance from the left edge and from the bottom edge).

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed horizontal width of the hanging display strip (same length unit as panel dimensions). Each panel's left offset plus its width must not exceed this value.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: An optional vertical limit for the strip (same units as panel heights). If provided, panels must lie entirely below this height; if not provided or set to a very large value it means the strip height is effectively unbounded and the goal is to minimize the used height instead.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a specific art panel. When placed, the panel's leftward offset plus this width must be ≤ the strip_width.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size of a specific art panel. A panel's top is its bottom offset plus this height; the maximum of those tops across all panels is the used height to minimize.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier or label for the panel type (used to reference each distinct panel that must be hung exactly once).

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The usable internal width of the display tray (distance from the tray's inner left wall to its inner right wall). Every sample's horizontal position (distance from left) plus its sample_width must lie within 0 .. tray_inner_width.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The vertical height limit of the tray measured from the interior bottom upward. If specified, no sample's top edge (bottom offset + sample_height) may exceed this value; in strip-packing instances this may be treated as unbounded (no strict limit) if not applicable.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a sample board (distance from its left edge to its right edge). When a sample is placed at an x offset from the tray left, its right edge is at x + sample_width and must not cross the tray_inner_width.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size of a sample board (distance from its bottom edge to its top edge). When a sample is placed at a y offset from the tray bottom, its top edge is at y + sample_height; the overall packing height is the maximum of these top edges.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for the sample board type (label or index). Exactly one copy of each sample_id must be placed in the tray.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: Interior horizontal width of the vertical display rack (distance from left to right inside edges). All box left offsets x must satisfy 0 <= x <= rack_width - box_width so boxes lie fully inside the rack.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: Interior vertical height limit of the display rack measured from the base to the top edge. If the rack has a fixed maximum height, this is that limit and every box top (vertical_offset + box_height) must be <= this value; if the rack height is unbounded for the instance, treat this field as not restricting placements.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: Horizontal size of the gift box (distance from its left face to its right face). Used to ensure the box fits inside the rack horizontally and to prevent horizontal overlap with other boxes.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: Vertical size of the gift box (distance from its bottom face to its top face). The top edge of a placed box is vertical_offset + box_height; the objective is to minimize the maximum of these top edges across all boxes.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for a specific gift box type (each box must be placed exactly once). Use this id to report the box's placement offsets from the rack's left edge and base.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: Total usable horizontal width of the storage ledge measured from the left edge to the right edge. Every plank's horizontal placement (distance from the left edge) plus its plank_width must be ≤ this value so the plank fits entirely within the ledge.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: Optional vertical limit of the ledge measured from the floor up to the top boundary. If provided, every plank's vertical placement (distance from the floor) plus its plank_height must be ≤ this value. If the ledge height is unbounded for the instance, this value may be omitted or set very large; regardless, the packing objective is to minimize the highest top edge (max of y + plank_height).

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: Horizontal length of a plank (parallel to the ledge). This is the distance the plank occupies left-to-right; when placing a plank at horizontal coordinate x, ensure x + plank_width ≤ shelf_width.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: Vertical thickness of a plank (parallel to the ledge floor). A plank placed at vertical coordinate y has its top at y + plank_height; the objective is to make the maximum of these top values as small as possible.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for the plank (name or index). Use this to refer to the specific plank when reporting its placement (distance from the left edge and distance from the floor to its bottom-left corner).

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed horizontal width of the mounting board (distance from left to right edge). All swatches' left offsets plus their widths must be ≤ this value; horizontal positions are measured from the board's left boundary.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The vertical height limit of the mounting board (distance from bottom to top edge). If the workshop treats height as unbounded this may be set to a large limit or ignored; otherwise all swatches' bottom offsets plus their heights must be ≤ this value. Vertical positions are measured from the board's bottom boundary.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a fabric swatch. Used to ensure the swatch fits within the board horizontally and to prevent horizontal overlap with other swatches when combined with its recorded left offset.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size of a fabric swatch. Combined with the swatch's bottom offset it determines the top edge (bottom offset + swatch_height) used to evaluate the total used board height and to prevent vertical overlap.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for the swatch (name or index). Associates each swatch with its specified width, height, and the recorded left and bottom offsets so the crew knows which swatch is placed where.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed horizontal width of the display strip (the distance from the left edge to the right edge). All tag left offsets must be between 0 and (display_strip_width - tag_width) so the tag stays inside the strip.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The vertical extent available for placing tags. In many instances this is an upper bound or a large number representing an effectively unbounded height; the objective is to minimize the maximum top edge used within this limit.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a single price tag. This determines how much horizontal space the tag occupies on the strip and constrains its allowable left offset so the tag remains fully inside the strip.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size of a single price tag. The bottom offset plus this height gives the tag's top position; the maximum of those top positions across all tags is the packing height to be minimized.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for the price tag type (label or index). Exactly one copy of each tag_id must be placed; used to report the left and bottom offsets for that specific tag.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed horizontal width of the kitchen wall panel (distance from the left edge to the right edge). Every recipe card's left-coordinate plus its card_width must not exceed this value.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: An optional upper limit on the panel's vertical extent. If specified, no card's bottom-coordinate plus its card_height may exceed this value. If left unbounded in the instance, it indicates the panel height is not pre-fixed and the solver should minimize the used height (the highest card top).

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a recipe card. Cards cannot be rotated, so this is the distance they occupy left-to-right and is used to ensure the card fits inside the panel width and does not overlap other cards horizontally.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size of a recipe card. A card placed at vertical position y reaches to y + card_height; the objective is to minimize the maximum of these top positions (subject to any panel_max_height).

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for each recipe card type (each card appears exactly once). Use this id when reporting the card's placement (distance from left edge and from bottom edge).

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed horizontal width of the vertical test stand (distance from left edge to right edge). All cabinet doors must fit within this width; a door's horizontal position (its bottom-left x-coordinate) plus its door_width cannot exceed this value.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The vertical height limit of the test stand, i.e., the maximum allowable distance from the bottom to the top edge inside which doors must lie. In some instances this may represent a true fixed height; if the stand height is unbounded for the instance, this field can be used as an upper bound or set to a large value. The arrangement's objective is to minimize the actual used height (the highest top edge of any door).

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a cabinet door measured left-to-right. When placing a door, its bottom-left x-coordinate plus this door_width determines its right edge; that right edge must not exceed test_stand_width.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size of a cabinet door measured bottom-to-top. A door's bottom-left y-coordinate plus this door_height gives its top edge; the maximum of those top edges across all doors is the used height to be minimized.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for each cabinet door (e.g., label or index). Use this id to specify the placement (bottom-left x and y) of exactly one instance of that door in the packing.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal width of the hanging rail (distance from the rail's left edge to its right edge). All canvases must be placed with their left-offset + canvas width ≤ rail_width. Measured in the same linear units used for canvas sizes.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The vertical limit of the hanging area measured from the rail base up to the top boundary. Canvases' bottom-offset + canvas height must not exceed this value. If the instance represents an unbounded vertical strip (no fixed top), this field may be null or set to a sentinel indicating unlimited height; otherwise it constrains feasible placements.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a canvas (its extent along the rail). Used to compute horizontal occupancy: left-offset + canvas_width is the canvas's right edge and must lie within the rail_width. Canvases are axis-aligned and cannot be rotated.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size of a canvas (distance from its bottom edge to its top edge). The packing objective uses these to compute the overall used height: the maximum, over all canvases, of (bottom-offset + canvas_height).

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for each canvas (e.g., a label or index). Identifies which canvas the reported left and bottom offsets refer to; exactly one placement must be provided for each canvas_id.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: Inner horizontal width of the vertical slot (distance from the left wall to the right wall). All mat board left-bottom x-coordinates plus their widths must lie within this value.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The overall vertical height of the packing: the highest y-coordinate reached by the top edge of any placed mat board (the quantity to be minimized). If the slot has a fixed maximum height, this represents the usable/occupied height; if height is unbounded, this is the objective value to minimize.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: Horizontal size of a mat board (its left–right extent). When placed, the board's bottom-left x-coordinate plus this width must not exceed the slot_width.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: Vertical size of a mat board (its bottom–top extent). When placed, the board's bottom-left y-coordinate plus this height contributes to the used_height.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for a mat board type or instance. Use this id when giving the board's bottom-left coordinates (distance from the left wall and from the bottom).

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed horizontal width of the wall strip (distance from the left boundary to the right boundary). All sample bottom-left x coordinates must be placed between 0 and wall_strip_width - sample_width so the sample lies fully inside the strip.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The available vertical height of the wall (an upper bound on how tall the packing may be). If the instance allows unbounded height, this value may be null or omitted; otherwise every sample's bottom-left y must be between 0 and wall_strip_height_limit - sample_height.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a fabric sample. Used to check horizontal fit inside the strip and to prevent horizontal overlap with other samples.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size of a fabric sample. A sample placed with bottom-left y has top edge at y + sample_height; the objective minimizes the maximum of these top edges.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for each fabric sample (for example a label or SKU). Exactly one instance of each sample_id must be placed on the wall.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed horizontal width of the workshop's stacking board (distance from the left edge to the right edge). Each pane's x-coordinate (its bottom-left corner) must be chosen so the pane lies entirely within [0, stacking_board_width].

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The vertical height available on the stacking board. Placements must satisfy 0 <= y and y + pane_height <= stacking_board_height. If the instance models an unbounded height, this field represents a sufficiently large or variable upper limit for feasible placements.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size (width) of a single window pane. Measured in the same units as the board; when placing a pane its x position must ensure the entire pane fits within the board width.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size (height) of a single window pane. The pane's top edge is at y + pane_height and contributes to the packing objective of minimizing the maximum top edge.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for the pane type (e.g., a label or index). Exactly one copy of each pane_id must be placed on the stacking board.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed horizontal width of the sticker roll (distance from left to right edge). Every sticker's horizontal position plus its width must not exceed this value; stickers are placed axis-aligned and cannot be rotated.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size limit of the roll (distance from bottom to top). In many instances this represents an upper bound on usable height (the packing objective is to minimize the actual used height, the maximum top edge of any sticker). If the instance uses unbounded height, treat this as a given upper bound for feasibility checks.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal dimension of a sticker. When placing a sticker, its bottom-left x-coordinate plus this value must be ≤ roll_width; rotation is not allowed.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical dimension of a sticker. When placing a sticker, its bottom-left y-coordinate plus this value determines its top edge; the objective is to minimize the maximum of these top edges across all stickers.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a sticker type (one copy of each identifier must be placed). Use this id to reference the sticker when assigning its bottom-left coordinates and enforcing non-overlap and boundary constraints.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: Width of the fixed wooden board in centimetres measured left-to-right. All shelf backings must fit horizontally within [0, board_width_cm]; for any backing its left x-coordinate plus its backing_width_cm must not exceed this value.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: Vertical extent of the board in centimetres measured from the bottom. This is the vertical limit that backings must not exceed; in strip-packing instances this may be an upper bound or set large if height is effectively unbounded. The packing objective is to minimize the highest top edge of any backing (the used height) which must be ≤ board_max_height_cm.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: Horizontal size of a single shelf backing in centimetres. Backings are axis-aligned and cannot be rotated, so each backing's x-position plus backing_width_cm must remain within the board_width_cm.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: Vertical size of a single shelf backing in centimetres. A backing placed with bottom y-coordinate has its top at y + backing_height_cm; the maximum of these top values across all backings is the used height to be minimized.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for each shelf backing type (e.g., a label or index). Exactly one copy of each backing_id must be placed on the board without overlap.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed horizontal width of the pallet area (distance from the pallet's left edge to its right edge). Each parcel's x (left) coordinate plus its parcel_width must not exceed this value.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: An optional upper bound on the usable vertical height of the pallet (distance from the pallet's bottom edge upward). If provided, every parcel's bottom y coordinate plus its parcel_height must be ≤ this limit. If absent or null, the pallet height is unbounded and the solver's objective is to minimize the maximum parcel top.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a parcel. When placed at horizontal position x, the parcel occupies [x, x + parcel_width) and must fit entirely within the pallet_width.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size (thickness) of a parcel. When placed at vertical position y (distance from the pallet bottom), the parcel's top is at y + parcel_height; the packing's cost is the maximum of these tops.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for each parcel type (one copy of each id must be placed). Used to refer to parcels when specifying their bottom-left (x,y) positions.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed horizontal width of the mounting strip in centimeters (distance from the left edge to the right edge). Each banner's horizontal bottom-left coordinate x must satisfy 0 ≤ x ≤ strip_width_cm - banner_width_cm so the banner lies fully inside the strip.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The vertical height limit (in centimeters) available on the strip. This is the upper bound for placements (top edges must be ≤ this value). If the instance models an unbounded strip, this field may be set to a large number representing no practical bound; the optimization objective is to minimize the actual used height (highest top edge).

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a banner in centimeters. This value is used to ensure the banner stays within the strip's left/right boundaries and to check horizontal non-overlap with other banners.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size of a banner in centimeters. The banner's top edge is at vertical coordinate (bottom_left_y + banner_height_cm); the objective cares about the maximum of these top edges.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for the banner type (e.g., a name or index). Exactly one banner with this identifier must be placed on the strip at some (x,y) bottom-left position.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed horizontal width of the wall strip (distance from the left wall edge to the right wall edge). All panels' bottom-left x-coordinate plus their panel_width must be ≤ this value.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The vertical extent available on the wall measured from the floor upward. When specified, this is the maximum allowed height for any panel placement (bottom-left y + panel_height ≤ strip_max_height). If the packing problem treats height as unbounded, this field may represent a reporting or bounding value rather than a strict limit.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a pattern panel. In placement, this determines how far the panel extends to the right from its bottom-left anchor (x). Must fit within the strip_width when positioned.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size of a pattern panel. In placement, this determines how far the panel extends upward from its bottom-left anchor (y). The objective minimizes the largest (y + panel_height) over all panels.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for the pattern panel type. Exactly one panel with this id must be placed; used to refer to each panel when specifying its bottom-left anchor and verifying non-overlap.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed horizontal width of the display shelf (distance from left to right edge). All props' horizontal placements and widths must fit inside this value.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: An optional vertical boundary for the shelf. If provided, props must lie entirely below this height; if the instance treats height as unbounded, this value may be omitted or treated as infinite. The packing objective is to minimize the highest top edge used.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a prop (how much distance it occupies left-to-right). Each prop's left-edge coordinate plus this width must not exceed the shelf_width.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size of a prop (how tall it is). The used height of the arrangement is the maximum, over all props, of each prop's bottom-edge coordinate plus this prop_height.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for this prop type (one copy of each identifier must be placed). Use this id to refer to the prop when specifying its placement coordinates.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: Fixed horizontal width of the shipping sleeve (distance from left to right). Every insert's left x-coordinate plus its width must not exceed this value; it is the strip's fixed bin width used to constrain x positions.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: Vertical extent available on the sleeve (distance from bottom to top). In 2D strip-packing instances this may be unbounded; if given, it is the maximum allowable used height so every insert's bottom y-coordinate plus its height must be ≤ this value. If unbounded, treat this as no fixed upper limit while minimizing the packing height.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: Horizontal size of the rectangular insert. This determines x-placement constraints: 0 ≤ x and x + insert_width ≤ sleeve_inner_width.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: Vertical size of the rectangular insert. Its top edge is at y + insert_height; the maximum of these top edges across all inserts is the packing's used height (objective). Must satisfy 0 ≤ y and y + insert_height ≤ sleeve_height_limit when a height limit is provided.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for the insert type (label or index). Exactly one copy of each insert_id must be placed on the sleeve and assigned bottom-left coordinates.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed horizontal width of the booth (distance from the left wall to the right wall). Every mat's horizontal placement x (distance from the left edge) must satisfy 0 ≤ x ≤ booth_width - mat_width so the mat lies fully inside the booth.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The vertical extent available for packing the mats. In some instances this may be unspecified (effectively unbounded). If provided, it is the maximum allowed top edge (y + mat_height) for any mat; if not provided, treat this as variable and the solver's objective is to minimize the actual used height, defined as the maximum top edge of any placed mat.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a single display mat type. This is the amount of horizontal space the mat occupies; when placed at horizontal coordinate x it spans [x, x + mat_width).

item_fields.name: height
