item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size (height) of a single display mat type. When the mat is placed at vertical coordinate y it spans [y, y + mat_height); the objective depends on the highest such top edge across all mats.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A short identifier for the mat type (each identifier denotes exactly one copy of that mat to place). Use this id to refer to the mat when giving its (x,y) bottom-left placement.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed usable left-to-right width of the bench (distance between the left and right rails). Every tray's horizontal position plus its tray_width must lie within this limit.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The available vertical clearance of the bench measured from the bench surface upward (top boundary). Every tray's vertical position plus its tray_height must not exceed this height; if the instance treats height as unbounded, this value represents the allowed or considered upper limit for placements.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The left-to-right size of a seed tray type. This must fit within the bench_width when placed and determines horizontal occupancy when setting the tray's bottom-left x-coordinate.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size (depth) of a seed tray type. When placed at a bottom-left y-coordinate, y + tray_height is the top edge whose maximum across all trays is the packing's used height.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a seed tray type (one copy of each tray_type_id must be placed). Use this id to refer to the tray when assigning its bottom-left coordinates on the bench.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: Width of the feeder strip measured left-to-right. Every print's horizontal position x plus its width must not exceed this value; x is measured from the left boundary.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: Maximum allowed height of the feeder measured bottom-to-top. If a finite value is provided, every print's vertical position y plus its height must not exceed this value. If the feeder height is unbounded for the instance, this field can be treated as unlimited and the solver should minimize the actual used height (the highest top edge).

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: Horizontal size of a single print job. When a job is placed at horizontal coordinate x (from the left), its right edge is at x + print_width and must lie within the strip_width.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: Vertical size of a single print job. When a job is placed at vertical coordinate y (from the bottom), its top edge is at y + print_height; the objective is to minimize the maximum of all jobs' top edges.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for the print job (string or number). Use this id to refer to the job when assigning its print_width, print_height, and placement coordinates (x,y).

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed horizontal width of the hanging strip (distance from the left edge to the right edge). Each board's bottom-left x coordinate must be ≥ 0 and its x + board_width must be ≤ strip_width.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The vertical extent used by the packing: the vertical coordinate of the highest top edge among all placed boards (this is the quantity the designer wants to minimize). If an upper bound on strip height is given it serves as a hard limit; otherwise treat packing_height as the optimization variable equal to max(y + board_height) over all boards.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a board (its width). Boards cannot be rotated, so this is the fixed extent in the x-direction used to check containment (x ∈ [0, strip_width - board_width]) and to enforce non-overlap horizontally with other boards.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size of a board (its height). The board's top edge is at y + board_height; packing_height is the maximum of these top-edge coordinates. Boards must lie fully within the strip in the y-direction (y ≥ 0 and, if applicable, y + board_height ≤ packing_height or the height bound).

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for each rectangular board design. Exactly one copy of each board_id must be placed on the strip, axis-aligned and non-overlapping with the others.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed horizontal width of the runner (distance from the runner's left edge to its right edge). Every panel's horizontal position x must satisfy x >= 0 and x + width <= runner_width.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The vertical dimension of the runner. In many instances this is unbounded; when provided it represents an upper bound on the allowed packing height. The actual objective is to minimize the used height, i.e., the maximum value of y + height over all placed panels.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a floor graphic panel. When the panel's left-edge is placed at horizontal offset x, its right edge is at x + panel_width and must not exceed runner_width.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size of a floor graphic panel. When the panel's bottom edge is placed at vertical offset y, its top edge is at y + panel_height; the packing's objective is to minimize the maximum of these top-edge values.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for each distinct floor graphic panel. Each panel_id refers to exactly one panel that must be placed once inside the runner without overlapping other panels.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The cutter's fixed usable width (left-to-right distance across the bed). Every pattern's left offset plus its pattern_width must not exceed this value; patterns cannot be rotated and must fit within this width.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The cutter's usable length in the stacking (front-to-back) direction if a hard upper limit exists. In many strip-packing instances this is effectively unbounded and should be set to a large value; otherwise every pattern's bottom offset plus its pattern_length must not exceed this limit.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The pattern's horizontal size across the bed (measured left-to-right). When placing a pattern, its left offset + pattern_width gives its right edge against the bed's usable width.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The pattern's size in the stacking (front-to-back) direction. A pattern's bottom offset + pattern_length gives its top edge; the maximum top edge over all patterns is the total used length to minimize.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for each fabric pattern type. Exactly one copy of each pattern_id must be placed on the bed without overlap.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: Inner width of the vertical storage slot (distance between left and right interior faces). Every panel's horizontal position plus its panel_width must lie within this span.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: Vertical capacity (maximum usable height) of the slot. If the slot is effectively unbounded for the instance, this can be set very large or treated as unlimited; the solver's objective remains to minimize the actual used height (highest panel top).

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: Horizontal size of a glass panel (how much of the slot width it occupies). When placed, the panel's left coordinate plus panel_width must not exceed slot_width.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: Vertical size of a glass panel (distance from its bottom edge to its top edge). The panel's bottom coordinate plus panel_height gives its top edge used to compute the packing height.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for this rectangular glass sheet type (one copy of each panel_id must be placed upright in the slot).

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed horizontal internal width of the rigid strip (distance from left to right border). All tile x-coordinates (bottom-left corner) must satisfy 0 ≤ x ≤ strip_width - tile_width; used to enforce horizontal containment and detect horizontal overlaps.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: An optional upper bound on the packing's vertical extent. If provided, every tile's top edge (y + tile_height) must be ≤ strip_height_limit. If null or absent, the strip height is unbounded and the solver's objective is to minimize the achieved used height (the maximum top edge over all tiles).

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a tile type. This is the amount added to a tile's x-position to obtain its right edge; must be positive and not exceed strip_width for feasible placement.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size of a tile type. This is the amount added to a tile's y-position to obtain its top edge; the objective is to minimize the maximum of y + tile_height over all placed tiles.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for a tile type. Exactly one instance of each tile_type_id must be placed on the strip; identifiers are used to reference tiles when assigning x and y coordinates and enforcing non-overlap and containment.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed horizontal width of the web sidebar (in the same units as block sizes). All content blocks must fit within this width; valid horizontal placements range from 0 (left edge) to sidebar_width − block_width.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The vertical height available for placing blocks in the sidebar. In typical strip-packing instances this may be effectively unbounded (you minimize the used height), but if provided this is the maximum allowed scrollable height — no block's top edge may exceed this value.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a single content block. It must be less than or equal to the sidebar_width and determines how far the block extends to the right from its left (horizontal) placement coordinate.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size of a single content block. A block placed at vertical coordinate y occupies [y, y + block_height); the packing objective is to minimize the highest such top edge across all blocks (the scroll length).

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for each content block type (for example 'logo', 'menu', 'ad', 'article_preview'). Exactly one block of each block_id must be placed in the sidebar.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: Horizontal width of the fixed shop display band (the left–right span). All item placements use this to ensure 0 <= x <= display_band_width - item_display_width so every merchandise display lies fully inside the band.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: Vertical capacity (height limit) of the display band. If the instance provides a finite value, every item must satisfy 0 <= y <= display_band_height_limit - item_display_height. If height is unbounded for packing, this field can be set very large or treated as not constraining placements; the objective remains minimizing the maximum (y + item_display_height).

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: Horizontal size of a merchandise display (how much left–right space it occupies). Must fit inside the band width and is used to compute allowable x (left-edge) positions so items do not cross the left/right boundaries.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: Vertical size of a merchandise display (how tall the rectangle is). Used to compute allowable y (bottom-edge) positions, to ensure items stay inside the band vertically, and to determine the overall used height (max y + item_display_height).

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for a particular merchandise display type (used to refer to its given width and height). Exactly one item of each merchandise_id must be placed with axis-aligned, non-overlapping bottom-left coordinates within the band.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed horizontal width of the plating rack (distance from left to right). Every plate's left x-coordinate plus its plate_width must lie within [0, rack_width]; no plate may extend beyond this width.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: An optional vertical limit for the rack (distance from bottom to top). If provided, no plate's top edge (y + plate_height) may exceed this value. If not provided or set very large, treat the rack height as effectively unbounded — the solver then minimizes the actual used height (the highest plate top).

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a single rectangular plate (left-to-right). Plate_width combined with the plate's x-position determines the plate's horizontal span inside the rack; it must be <= rack_width when placed.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size of a single rectangular plate (bottom-to-top). Plate_height together with the plate's y-position determines the plate's top edge (y + plate_height), which is used to compute the packing's used height to be minimized.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for each plate type (e.g., part number or label). Used to refer to that specific plate when assigning its x and y placement and dimensions; exactly one plate instance of each plate_id must be placed.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed interior width of the corridor display measured left-to-right; every plank's horizontal extent (its width) must fit within this distance when placed from the left edge.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The vertical extent available for the display measured bottom-to-top. This is the maximum allowed packing height (when treated as a bound); in the usual minimization view the actual used height is the highest top edge of any plank and should be as small as possible.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a single flooring plank (distance from its left edge to right edge); determines how much corridor width the plank occupies and must be respected so the plank fits between the left boundary and corridor_width.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size of a single flooring plank (distance from its bottom edge to top edge); contributes to the top edge used by the arrangement and thus to the objective of minimizing overall display height.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for each rectangular plank design (each sample board). Exactly one plank with this identifier must be placed in the corridor.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: Fixed left-to-right width of the wooden sheet/board onto which templates are laid. All templates must lie within this width; a template's bottom-left x-coordinate must be between 0 and board_width - template_width.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The vertical measurement from the bottom of the board up to the highest top edge of any placed template. This is the effective packing height the carpenter wants to minimize. (If an upper bound on sheet height is provided in the instance it limits placements; otherwise this field records the objective value.)

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: Horizontal size of a door template (distance left-to-right). Used to ensure the template fits inside the board width when choosing its bottom-left x-coordinate.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: Vertical size of a door template (distance bottom-to-top). A template placed at vertical coordinate y has its top at y + template_height, which determines contribution to used_sheet_height.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: Unique identifier for a specific door template/type. Exactly one template with each door_id must be placed on the board, axis-aligned and non-overlapping with others.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed horizontal width of the portrait column in the studio layout. Every photo is placed upright (no rotation) and its left offset plus its photo_width must not exceed this column_width.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The available vertical extent of the column. If a finite value is given, every photo's bottom offset plus its photo_height must fit within this height; if unspecified or effectively infinite, treat the column as having no preset top and minimize the used height instead.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a single portrait print when placed upright. This is how much space the photo consumes left-to-right and must satisfy left_offset >= 0 and left_offset + photo_width <= column_width.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size of a single portrait print. The photo's top edge is at bottom_offset + photo_height and the maximal such top edge over all photos defines the used height of the packing to be minimized.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for each portrait print type (each distinct photo size). Exactly one copy of each photo_id must be placed somewhere in the column without overlap.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed horizontal width of the street-pole banner (distance between the banner's left and right edges). Each poster's left offset plus its poster_width must not exceed this value; posters are placed upright and flush within these edges.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: The vertical extent of the banner. If no fixed upper limit is given, this denotes the used banner height that the solver minimizes (the highest top edge of any poster). If a maximum allowable banner height is specified, this represents that upper boundary posters must not exceed.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a single poster for an event. When placing a poster, its left offset plus this poster_width must lie within banner_width; posters remain upright (no rotation) and aligned with the banner edges.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size of a single poster. A poster's bottom placement plus this poster_height gives its top edge; the objective is to minimize the maximum such top edge across all posters (the banner's used height).

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: The identifier for the poster/event (for example, an event name or numeric ID). Exactly one poster for each event_id must be placed on the banner.

global_fields.name: bin_width
global_fields.scenario_description: The fixed usable width of the laminating roll (horizontal span from left to right). All sheet bottom-left x coordinates must be >= 0 and each sheet's x + sheet_width must be <= this strip_width. Measured in the same linear units as sheet dimensions.

global_fields.name: bin_height
global_fields.scenario_description: An optional upper bound on the vertical space available on the roll (distance from bottom edge upward). In some instances this is unbounded and only used as a planning limit; otherwise all sheet bottom-left y coordinates must be >= 0 and each sheet's y + sheet_height must be <= this strip_height_limit. The objective, when not fixed, is to minimize the maximum y + sheet_height reached by any sheet.

item_fields.name: width
item_fields.scenario_description: The horizontal size of a veneer sheet measured parallel to the roll edges. Sheets cannot be rotated, so this value is the extent in x-direction that must fit within strip_width.

item_fields.name: height
item_fields.scenario_description: The vertical size of a veneer sheet measured parallel to the roll edges. This value determines how far the sheet extends above its placed bottom-left y coordinate and contributes to the packing's used height.

item_fields.name: item_type
item_fields.scenario_description: A unique identifier for the sheet type (one rectangular veneer of this size). Exactly one copy of each sheet_type_id must be placed on the roll; identifiers link each sheet to its sheet_width and sheet_height.
